artboards.title: Variation A, flowchart with trust lanes

annotations.text: Working set, unchanged look. QueryFlow gained the route-traceability card you asked for. The originals before this round are saved in diagram/v1 and in git.

A. Classic flowchart, swimlanes by trust: deterministic, model assisted, human.
Wins: reads instantly as an architecture, inputs and outputs explicit, shows at a glance where nondeterminism lives and that models are optional to correctness.
Trade: less prose depth on the sheet itself, the speaker notes and deep-dive pages carry it.

B. Keep the current five-column shape but compress it to a strip, and spend the sheet on six numbered decision callouts, the FP and FN cost asymmetry, refuse-before-guess, derive-then-diff, the trust gradient, scale.
Wins: your cleverest thinking becomes the visual centrepiece, numbered anchors to point at live.
Trade: text-heavy, the pipeline itself is only a summary strip.

C. A clean overview sheet backed by one deep-dive page per pipeline area. This is the ingestion sample, intake, rulebook and fit checks, the extraction ladder, parse and assemble, with concrete examples from the document on every card.
Wins: room for every idea with examples, nothing lost, jargon decoded in place.
Trade: a multi-page deliverable, more to maintain and print.
Mix and match is fine, for example A as the overview plus C pages behind it, with B's callouts folded into either.
